styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Casco Antiguo, Panama Viejo ruins and the canal story.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Rainforest, monkeys and the Causeway on the water.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Ceviche, sancocho and markets in the old town.

stays.why: Walk to plazas, churches and restaurants. Best for first-time sightseeing and evenings out.
Central, good-value hotels and many cafés. Easy metro and taxi access to both old town and canal.
Near the waterfront and Calle Uruguay dining. A short taxi to Casco Antiguo.
Water views and quiet nights. Good for walks and bike rides; further from the old town.

food: Try Panamanian dishes: ceviche, sancocho (chicken soup) and ropa vieja. Lunch sets are often B/.8–15.
Mercado de Mariscos by the fish market: cheap fresh seafood, best at lunch.
Casco Antiguo has many small restaurants and rooftop bars; book ahead on weekends.
Cafés in El Cangrejo and Bella Vista are good for breakfast; expect B/.5–10.
Street snacks like empanadas and patacones cost a few balboas. Drink bottled water.
more_time: Add a day for the Panama Canal Miraflores locks and the museum; check opening hours on the day.
Swap a city afternoon for Soberanía National Park or the Metropolitan Natural Park for rainforest and birds.
Take a day trip to the causeway islands or a boat on the canal; confirm prices locally.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the old town, the canal and one nature day without rushing in the heat.

month_notes: Dry season starts: warm days, about 8 rain days. Good for walking the old town.
Driest month, about 5 rain days. Best time for canal and outdoor sights.
Still fairly dry, about 9 rain days. Warm and busy around Carnival.
Wet season begins: about 19 rain days. Plan mornings outside, afternoons indoors.
Very wet, about 29 rain days. Carry a rain jacket and keep plans flexible.
Wet and humid, about 29 rain days. Short heavy showers most days.
Wet season continues, about 29 rain days. Similar to June; pack quick-dry clothes.
Very wet, about 30 rain days. Expect afternoon downpours.
Wettest stretch, about 30 rain days. Indoor museums and cafés are safer bets.
Still wet, about 29 rain days. Rain often clears; check forecasts daily.
Rain eases slightly, about 28 rain days. Still humid and showery.
Dry season returns: about 19 rain days. Good value and improving weather.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical climate: hot all year, with a dry season roughly December to April and a very wet season May to November.

items.title: Best time: January to March
items.text: Highs 30–32°C and only 5–9 rain days. Best for the canal, old town and nature walks.

items.title: Wet season May to November
items.text: Rain on 28–30 days most months. Showers are often heavy but pass; plan indoor backups.

items.title: Hot and humid year-round
items.text: Lows stay near 24–25°C. Drink water and take midday breaks.

items.title: Pack rain gear
items.text: A light rain jacket or umbrella helps from May to November.

items.title: Mosquitoes in the wet months
items.text: Use repellent for parks and evenings, especially May to November.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, sun hat, sunscreen, rain layer and comfortable walking shoes.

transit.best: Metro for main routes; taxis or ride apps for the old town and canal.

modes.text: Line 1 runs underground from Albrook to El Ingenio; Line 2 serves the northern suburbs. Fare B/.0.35 on Line 1 and B/.0.50 on Line 2; last train about 22:00.
Metrobuses need a RapiPass card (about B/.2 plus top-up); cash is not accepted at turnstiles.
Taxis have no meter; fares are zone-based, roughly B/.1.25 in one zone up to B/.5 across town. Uber and inDrive work; agree the price before a street taxi ride.
Useful for day trips outside the city; city traffic is busy. Check parking at your hotel.
Good in Casco Antiguo and along the Causeway. Use taxis for longer hops in the heat.
